turn.subject: solution
turn.user_message: Show me who is in charge

text: You need one person to own discharge, and two people to run it day to day. Why:
bullets: Nobody owns the whole wait today, and your own numbers are past the lines where one owner is needed.
Two helpers, not three, because your work comes in two busy times of day, not spread across 24 hours.
Every other team only records and approves a little more. Their jobs don’t change.
chat.invite: Last part: how we’ll know it worked. Shall we go there?
chat.note: One owner, two helpers, sized to your busy hours.

blocks.title: One owner, two helpers

items.title: Discharge Manager
items.text: Owns the whole process, from the evening decision to the empty bed.
more_points: One person answers for every delay, instead of each team blaming the process.
Works with the bed desk manager as an equal. Both report to the Head of Operations.
Needed above 80% of beds full, 40 patients a day, or regular delays. Two of these apply to you.

items.title: Discharge Executives
items.text: Look after each patient going home, and chase every delay.
more_points: Take over each patient from the moment the doctor decides on the evening round.
Spot delays as they happen, and chase the team holding things up.
About ₹3 to 3.5 lakh a year each.

rows.label: How it is sized
values: One helper for every 15 patients a day

values: 7 PM round, then 11 AM to about 3 PM
